title: Frame a problem with evidence
setting: Fictional pilot; 8 adult colleagues; discovery only

segments.title: Purpose and participation
segments.instructions: We will leave with an evidence-linked problem frame and one open question. We are not selecting a solution today.
segments.fallback: Read the purpose and contribute in writing.

segments.title: Model a problem frame
segments.instructions: Review the fictional library signup example. Mark an observation and an assumption.

segments.title: Think and compare
segments.instructions: Write alone for two minutes; compare in pairs for four; record differences for two.
segments.fallback: Work solo or exchange in shared text.

segments.title: Form small groups
segments.instructions: Join another pair and retain each original note.
segments.fallback: Remain seated; exchange notes without moving.

segments.title: Inspect evidence
segments.instructions: For each claim identify support, contradiction, or missing evidence.
segments.fallback: Use a plain table rather than a digital board.

segments.title: Pause
segments.instructions: Take three minutes. Written notes remain available.

segments.title: Revise the frame
segments.instructions: Write the affected person, task, barrier, evidence, and remaining unknown.
segments.fallback: Dictate to a partner or write privately.

segments.title: Compare frames
segments.instructions: Share one difference that changes interpretation. Keep original statements separate.

segments.title: Reflect
segments.output: One changed interpretation and next question
segments.instructions: What evidence changed your frame? Then name one question worth checking.

segments.title: Capture the result
segments.purpose: Make status and next step explicit
segments.instructions: Confirm the frame and unresolved question. Record proposed ownership; no commitment is assumed.
segments.fallback: Send no messages; leave the local receipt ready.
